Accepted with zero wrong attempts.", path='arc-patterns', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T09:59:11.608614+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T10:56:19.392215+00:00', version=7), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_bcca5002_shift_foreground_down_one_row', kind='memory', title='ARC task-bcca5002: shift foreground down one row', content='For ARC task-bcca5002, the entire foreground pattern translates downward by exactly one cell while the grid dimensions and background remain unchanged. This adds another confirmation for large, irregular single-color patterns.', path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T11:08:15.666207+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T11:37:05.022828+00:00', version=3), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_8a59eaa1_repeat_motif_across_divider_separated_panels', kind='memory', title='ARC task-8a59eaa1: repeat motif across divider-separated panels', content='For ARC task-8a59eaa1, color-3 full rows/columns divide a grid into equal panels (in the demo, a full color-3 row and column made four equal quadrants). Make every panel identical by copying the non-background motif from the populated reference panel into the other panels, preserving within-panel coordinates and colors while leaving divider lines unchanged. In the solved test, color-3 rows 6 and 13 divided a 20x7 grid into three 6x7 panels. The last panel had a motif in local rows 0..5; the correct output copied that exact motif (including color-5 cells on color-2 background, plus colors 6 and 7) into both upper panels.

Additional accepted test: a 23x5 grid used color 2 full dividers at column 2 and rows 7 and 15, making six 7x2 panels on color-1 background. The middle-right panel contained the motif at panel-local coordinates (0,1)=3, (1,0)=6, (1,1)=6, (3,0)=9, and (5,1)=8. Make all six panels identical by copying this exact motif to the corresponding local positions in the other five panels; leave all color-2 divider cells and other background cells unchanged. This output was accepted on the first submission. Dividers need not be color 3; infer the background and uniform separator color from the input.

Additional accepted test: the 17x11 grid had color-4 full divider rows 5,11 and columns 3,7, creating nine 5x3 panels on color-1 background. The center-left panel contained a sparse motif at local coordinates (0,2)=7, (1,0)=9, (2,1)=7. Copy those cells with the same local coordinates/colors into all nine panels, preserving dividers and background; accepted on first submission. Thus the rule applies to a grid of 3x3 equal panels as well as 2x2 or 3x2 panels, and the source panel can be any one of them.', path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T11:07:09.588734+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T11:11:15.003331+00:00', version=3), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_3375ff3f_restore_noisy_rectangles', kind='memory', title='ARC task-3375ff3f: restore noisy solid rectangles', content='For ARC task-3375ff3f (repeated noisy-rectangle task), reconstruct every solid axis-aligned rectangular color block and remove isolated noise. The grid background is usually the dominant color; real blocks can be multiple different colors (including 0), and can be as small as 2x2. A rectangle may contain isolated cells of arbitrary noise colors or background-colored holes; fill its full bounding rectangle with the block color. Set all unrelated/noise cells outside rectangles to background. Do not assume only one foreground color, and do not require a block to be large. Carefully inspect every row when finding each rectangle’s full extent: this test had a large 8 block extending through row 10 while another 8 rectangle began at row 10 in separate columns; omitting that one row caused incorrect submissions.

Accepted task test, 0-indexed geometry (background 2): 8 blocks r0-1 c0-1; r1-3 c12-14; r4-10 c1-7; r6-8 c12-17; r10-14 c9-14; r12-13 c18-19. 9 blocks r0-2 c6-7; r0-1 c18-19; r3-4 c9-10; r13-14 c3-5. Fill those rectangles, set all other cells to 2. Corruptions inside blocks included 0/1/5/6, and isolated noise included 5 at r7c10, 0 at r10c18 and r11c0. Note r14c5=0 was a corruption inside the 9 block.

Demos also establish that small 2x2 blocks are legitimate (demo 4, color 7 at r7-8 c0-1); do not discard them merely for small area. Demo patterns showed several different block colors in one grid and isolated stray singletons of other colors should be reset. Previously summarized accepted example: background 0, 8 rectangles r2-5 c2-6, r3-6 c9-12, r8-9 c7-13; 1 rectangles r0-6 c14-16, r1-2 c22-27, r4-9 c18-23, r4-8 c25-29, r7-11 c2-5. All coordinates 0-indexed, bounding rectangles inclusive.

Accepted task test 2 (background 3): blocks were 4 rectangles r0-4 c0-2; r2-7 c5-8; r10-16 c4-6; 1 rectangle r1-6 c10-11; 5 rectangle r9-11 c8-9; 8 rectangle r13-18 c10-11. Isolated noise colors 2/9 were restored to the block color when within a rectangle, otherwise to background 3. Example: r0c1=2 was inside the 4 rectangle and became 4; r0c3=2 was outside and became 3. Use the bounding boxes of same-color solid rectangles to classify noise; multiple blocks can have same color, and their row spans may touch/overlap while columns remain separate.

Accepted test example (background 2, 13x15): output consists of three solid 6 rectangles: rows 1-4, cols 5-7; rows 3-4, cols 9-12; rows 6-10, cols 5-10 (0-indexed, inclusive). All other cells are 2. Input included isolated noise outside blocks and corruptions within these rectangles (e.g. 7, 3, 8, 4, 0); fill the rectangles with 6 and reset outside noise to background.

Additional accepted test (18x24, background 2): restore five rectangles of color 5 at r0-6 c8-11, r8-14 c4-7, r10-11 c9-13, and r9-11 c17-19, plus two color-9 rectangles at r3-6 c17-18 and r14-17 c11-16 (0-indexed inclusive). Fill all rectangle cells, including corrupted cells/holes (noise colors 0,1,3,4,6,8); set all other noise cells to 2. This confirms arbitrary noise colors are handled by location: within rectangle => rectangle color, outside => background.

Additional accepted test (26x29, background 1): restore a 3x3 color-7 rectangle at rows 2-4, cols 9-11 (it had a 0 at r2c10); a 3x6 color-3 rectangle at rows 21-23, cols 10-15 (it had a 0 at r22c14); and a 2x3 color-5 rectangle at rows 22-23, cols 3-5. Set all isolated noise cells to background 1, including the 8 adjacent to the 5 block. Submitted correctly after filling the two rectangle anomalies with their block colors. This supports locating blocks from the complete rectangle pattern and classifying speckles by whether they lie inside or outside a block.

Additional accepted test (18x23, background 6): restore color-3 rectangle r0-4 c3-7; color-7 rectangles r2-6 c14-19, r10-11 c4-9, and r11-12 c18-19; color-2 rectangle r15-16 c7-13 (0-indexed, inclusive). Reset all other cells, including isolated colors 1/4/5/8/9, to 6. Noise examples: r5c3 and r5c6=4, r11c6=8 inside the color-7 r10-11/c4-9 rectangle, r11c17=8 adjacent to but outside the 2x2 color-7 block, and r6c20=5. Correct output was accepted. This further confirms 2x2 rectangles are valid and noises are classified by bounding-box inclusion.', path='arc-patterns', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T10:09:03.303501+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T10:22:34.860134+00:00', version=7), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_252fc367_recolor_farthest_repeated_shape', kind='memory', title='ARC task-252fc367: recolor farthest copy of repeated shape', content="For ARC task-252fc367, identify the large L-shaped marker object (its color is the destination color). Find a shape that occurs in multiple disconnected components (components can have different colors), then recolor the copy farthest from the marker to the marker color; preserve all other cells. The farthest copy may be selected among congruent shapes such as single pixels, repeated irregular blobs, or repeated components. Evidence: demo 2 has two congruent 2-colored shapes and the farther/top-left one becomes marker color 7; demo 8 selects the farther singleton and recolors it to marker color 1. Solved test: marker 2 at upper-right; two identical 11-cell shapes were the 0 block at rows 2-5 cols 16-18 and the 8 blob at rows 0-3 cols 24-26; the farther 0 component became 2. Keep all remaining pixels unchanged. Additional solved test: a 13-cell 1-colored L marker sat at lower-right (rows 19-24, cols 21-28). Two translated identical 17-cell shapes, both initially color 3, were at rows 13-16/cols 10-15 and rows 21-24/cols 23-28; recolor the farther upper-left copy (rows 13-16, cols 10-15) to marker color 1. Other components remain unchanged. This confirms exact translated shape matching and greatest spatial distance from the marker, not recoloring the nearby copy.
Additional solved test (19x17): marker is color 6, a 10-cell thick L at rows 1-7, cols 1-4 (1-based). The duplicated shape is a 3-cell L triomino of color 7: near copy at rows 1-2/cols 1-2, far copy at rows 13-14/cols 14-15. Recolor only the far copy to 6. The near copy touches the marker but is a separate component; compare congruent component silhouettes and recolor the one farther from the marker, not the nearest. Submitted correct.
Additional solved test (24x16): guide is the color-7 L at rows 0-6, cols 12-15 (vertical leg col 12, bottom row 6). Two congruent L triominoes have different colors: color 8 at {(2,7),(3,7),(3,8)} and color 3 at {(3,14),(4,14),(4,15)} (0-indexed). Recolor only the farther color-8 triomino to 7; the color-3 triomino is near/within the guide's bounding box and stays unchanged. Other 8 components and all other cells remain unchanged. Submitted correct.
Additional solved test (20x26): guide is a 12-cell color-9 L at rows 0-4/cols 18-25 (vertical at col 18 through row 4, horizontal across row 4). Two identical 7-cell irregular components (same normalized silhouette) are color 7 at rows 0-2, cols 21-24 and rows 16-18, cols 5-8. Recolor only the far lower-left copy (rows 16-18, cols 5-8: cells {(16,6),(16,7),(16,8),(17,6),(18,5),(18,6),(18,7)}, 0-indexed) to 9; leave the top-right copy and every other cell unchanged. Submitted correct.
Additional solved test (19x14; important guide distinction): the true marker was the large 9-cell color-4 L at rows 13-18, cols 10-13 (0-indexed), not the smaller 5-cell color-8 L at rows 8-11, cols 3-4. The repeated 6-cell asymmetric shape occurred as color 8 at {(13,8),(13,9),(14,8),(14,9),(15,8),(16,8)} and color 7 at {(15,12),(15,13),(16,12),(16,13),(17,12),(18,12)}. Recolor the farther/outside-marker-bbox copy (the color-8 lower-left component) to marker color 4; preserve the color-7 copy. This was accepted. Caution: when both a small L and a larger L-shaped component appear, use the large marker object, not merely the first L-shaped component encountered. Match components by exact silhouette/translation; don't include an unrelated shape that only looks similar under non-translation reflection.
Additional solved test (14x23; 0-indexed): The marker is the color-5 9-cell L at rows 10-13, with horizontal arm across row 10, cols 18-22 and vertical leg at col 18. Recolor the farther of the translated 2x3 solid rectangles: the bottom-left color-1 rectangle at rows 12-13, cols 5-7 becomes 5; keep the bottom-right color-7 rectangle at rows 12-13, cols 20-22. Preserve everything else. There were also several horizontal dominoes, which were distractors; neither the bottom-right rectangle nor the far horizontal domino was the target. Important: identify the largest L-shaped guide itself and use its color as the destination; a separate prominent color-9 vertical/L-like component and detached color-9 bar are not the marker. I first incorrectly treated color 9 as the guide and both submissions failed; after recognizing the true color-5 L, the result was correct.
", path='arc-patterns', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T09:14:02.713363+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T10:05:14.051327+00:00', version=8), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_2fd86235_extract_colors_from_grid_cell_corners', kind='memory', title='ARC task-2fd86235: extract colors from grid-cell corners', content='For ARC task-2fd86235, the input is a large regular lattice: a base fill color occupies broad rectangles; thin horizontal/vertical separator lines of another color form cells; some line intersections are recolored. Build a coarse output by considering each rectangle between adjacent horizontal and vertical separator lines. If all four corner intersections have the same color and that color is not the separator-line color, output that corner color; otherwise use the broad interior fill color. Then trim all-background outer rows/columns (do not remove internal background gaps). Example: a coarse 2x4 intersection matrix [[6,6,8,8],[6,6,8,8]] with separator color 8 and fill color 3 yields cell matrix [[6,3,3]], then trim trailing all-3 columns to obtain [[6]]. A caution: returning the untrimmed matrix [[6,3,3]] or treating the separator color 8 as a special output gives the wrong result. Demonstrations support this: a grid of lines around blocks reduces to cell colors when all four corners match a non-separator marker; blank cells become the fill color. Crop rows/columns made entirely of the fill color at the outer edge.', path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T09:42:25.546094+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T09:42:25.546109+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_task_8a59eaa1_copy_one_quadrant_across_cross_divided_grid', kind='memory', title='ARC task-8a59eaa1: copy one quadrant across cross-divided grid', content='For ARC task-8a59eaa1, the grid has a background and a full horizontal/vertical cross of divider color, creating four equal rectangular regions. Preserve the cross separators. In the demonstration, a 29x5 grid had two horizontal separator rows and a 9x5 source panel; the exact panel was repeated into all three panels. In the test, the upper-right 6x6 quadrant was copied unchanged to upper-left, lower-left, and lower-right.', path='general', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-20T11:10:40.796358+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-20T11:10:40.796370+00:00', version=1)]
